articles.title: At 19, founder raises $11M for Ghost, maker of a $3,499 computer for personal AI | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Ghost's first product is Core, a personal computer designed specifically for AI agents that can take actions on a person's behalf.
articles.body_text: For much of his life, Zain Javaid, 19, wanted to be a quant who uses math and data to guide his investment decisions. And for a while, he was one. But he got bored. Then, in 2022, ChatGPT was released, and he told TechCrunch, “I felt fundamentally excited in a way that I never had been before.” He became interested in personal AI, and that interest led him to start Ghost, which announced Monday that it has emerged from stealth after a year of building, along with an $11 million seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz. Other investors in the round include Abstract, Audacious Ventures, SV Angel, and Nova. His founding team includes Nicholas Chua, 19, Yifei Chen, 24, and Gautam Sharda, 23. Ghost’s first product is Core, a personal computer designed specifically for AI agents that can take actions on a person’s behalf. According to Javaid, the idea is to centralize a person’s data, from what’s on their desktop to apps to smart home devices, into one piece of hardware designed to continuously run AI agents that can act as an assistant, perform tasks, and understand a person’s life. “You can run models on existing hardware, but it’s a terrible experience on many levels,” said Javaid, who is also Core’s CEO. Core includes an Nvidia RTX Pro 4000 SFF Blackwell GPU (a type of chip commonly used to run AI models), said Javaid, adding that the GPU is bundled into the device’s price, so customers don’t need to buy one separately. He said it also has its own software layer, browser, and filing system and can continuously process information and tasks without constant prompting. Core costs $3,499. Preorders for the first batch open Monday, and shipping is scheduled for the last week of October. Javaid described Core as a “brain in a box” without a screen, which users access through a phone or app. Voice mode is also available, but users must speak into the Core app rather than the box itself. Core comes with three models preinstalled: Qwen-3.8-Next, Qwen-3.8-27B, and Gemma-4-31B. Javaid said users can also install other models from Hugging Face, where developers share AI models, or load their own trained models. Asked how Core differs from a Mac Mini, Apple’s small desktop computer that some people set up to run AI tools, Javaid said Core’s hardware and software were built specifically for running AI agents, with models already installed, while the Mac Mini is a general-purpose computer that can be configured for AI. “As new models or improvements to existing models come out, we can push out over-the-air updates, similar to how Tesla works,” Javaid said of Core, adding that if a new generation of models comes out, the company asks users whether they want to switch. “Users can also turn on auto-updates so they’re always running the latest generation of a given model.” The team currently builds the units at its San Francisco facility. Javaid said the goal is to sell a fully functioning computer that doesn’t require complex setup or configuration. He said the models and personal memory run locally, and that all personal information is encrypted so that no cloud provider or third party, including Ghost, can meaningfully access it. He also said users can control how much autonomy they give their Core agents, and that the device is programmed to keep working if Ghost shuts down. “All of the source code, logic, and model weights live on the device, not the services,” he said. “We build this device to not be dependent on having an outside entity maintaining the service.” He said the team is also building a firewall to limit how the agent can use its credentials, such as logins and passwords. The firewall “monitors every outgoing network request on the computer and if it sees the agent performing a sanctioned action or exfiltrating data it shouldn’t, it rejects the request and flags it for user review.” “The user owns all of it,” he said of the device, memory, and data. “Once you buy the hardware, everything is stored, run, and processed on the device.” He said he is not too worried about the competition, including from established tech companies. “People sometimes give incumbents credit for having already built the product because they have the ingredients,” he said. He credited Apple with good hardware and disruption, but said much of what Core is aiming to tackle is software: “The model reasons over your life, how it remembers, how it takes action, how it knows when to reach out,” he continued.

articles.title: Hot Girl Hotline is like 'Dear Abby' for the AI era | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Founded by two sisters, Hot Girl Hotline uses AI to give young women personalized dating and relationship advice, with an emphasis on safety and avoiding emotional dependency.
articles.body_text: Women throughout history have always sought out relationship advice, whether from newspaper columnists like “Dear Abby,” letters to Cosmo, or just chatting with girlfriends. In the social media era, you can instead post anonymously on Reddit relationship forums or look to social media creators who discuss the topic. Now, two sisters are launching a startup for young women, Hot Girl Hotline , which focuses on bringing AI into these conversations. I know what you may be thinking: With all the advances in AI technology, founders are building something for women to talk about their dating woes? Well … yes! The reality is that people have already been turning to large language models (LLMs) via apps like ChatGPT for this type of advice, and the team believes this type of activity should be handled more carefully. Unfortunately, as we’ve seen, chatting with a general-purpose chatbot about personal topics can sometimes lead to disastrous effects — especially for those who were already mentally fragile. ChatGPT, for example, has faced a wave of lawsuits over its alleged manipulative conversation tactics that plaintiffs say contributed to negative mental health effects, including, in some cases, suicide. The idea behind Hot Girl Hotline is to reach young women who are looking to have these sorts of private conversations while navigating dating life and relationships, but in a safer way. “We’re not trying to be an AI companion,” explained Baila Mudgil , formerly a social media consultant, who co-founded the startup with her sister Sumrin (“Sumi”), who studied computer science at Stanford. “A companion is really going after solving loneliness, escapism, boredom — and you can rely on a lot of emotional dependency from that AI companion.” Baila says the startup’s approach is to focus on offering quality advice grounded in behavioral science, but in a way that makes it feel like you’re chatting with a trusted friend or big sister. The conversation is often Socratic, with the AI asking you questions to help you arrive at the answer yourself. “This is not to replace speaking to a human. This is not clinical advice, and we have a lot of safeguards in place … we take safety really seriously,” Baila said. If conversations raise flags, for instance, the user is referred to resources such as the crisis hotline 988. “We believe the key to quality advice is not just knowing what to do next; it’s understanding why you’re doing it. So that’s a big piece of it,” added Sumi. Notably, the AI also knows when to end the conversation; it doesn’t keep asking follow-up questions to drag you further down a rabbit hole. Instead, it pushes users to go take action out in the real world rather than ruminate on the problem. The sisters believe there’s room for an app like this because not everyone wants to post on the web for advice, and there are times when you don’t want to bring up a personal, dating, or relationship-focused issue with a friend.

articles.title: HackerRank's AI interviewer offers a glimpse into what job interviews could become | TechCrunch
articles.summary: HackerRank’s AI interviewer has already conducted more than 500,000 interviews, with Snowflake, Snorkel, and Capgemini among its early testers.
articles.body_text: What happens when AI moves from helping job candidates to evaluating them? HackerRank , a platform used by companies to assess and hire developers, is offering a glimpse at what that future of job interviews could look like with Chakra , an AI agent that conducts interviews, observes candidates as they work, and evaluates not just their answers but also how they got there. After around six months in beta, HackerRank is making Chakra generally available to its customers on Monday. The startup says the AI interviewer has already conducted more than 500,000 interviews during testing, with companies including Snowflake, Snorkel, and Capgemini among those that tried it, while HackerRank also tested the product internally. AI has been a staple in job interviews for some time , with companies using voice agents and other automated tools to screen candidates and make the hiring process more efficient. Job seekers, meanwhile, have increasingly gained their own AI tools to help them navigate interviews, sometimes without employers knowing. With Chakra, HackerRank is betting AI can change not only how interviews are conducted, but also what employers can measure. Beyond whether someone arrives at the right answer, the startup wants to assess harder-to-capture signals such as critical thinking and judgment, as well as what it calls “AI fluency” — how well a candidate frames a problem for AI, judges its output, and steers it toward a solution. “The previous modality of evaluation was evaluating the output,” HackerRank co-founder and CEO Vivek Ravisankar said in an interview. “Now, because of AI, anybody can produce an artifact.” The question for employers, he said, becomes whether they can understand the thinking and judgment that went into producing it. In practice, a Chakra interview is designed to look more like doing the job than taking a traditional coding test. A candidate gets a task involving a real-world code repository, and they work through it in a canvas that includes an AI assistant. As the candidate works, Chakra can use the context of what they are doing to ask follow-up questions, such as why they chose one approach over another, or how their solution would change if a new constraint were introduced. Ravisankar told TechCrunch that Chakra is changing the basic structure of the hiring process itself. What previously involved three separate rounds, comprising a recruiter screen, take-home assessment, and follow-up interview with an engineer, is now combined into a single Chakra interview, he said. Giving candidates access to AI during an interview might seem to make it easier to cheat. However, HackerRank says it found the opposite. Suspicious-activity flags, Ravisankar said, were 70% to 80% lower in Chakra interviews than in comparable traditional HackerRank assessments, though the rate varied depending on factors such as geography and seniority. Ravisankar told TechCrunch that giving candidates access to AI reduces the incentive to secretly use outside tools that can feed them answers during an interview. Launched at TechCrunch Disrupt in 2012, HackerRank built its business around coding challenges, eventually helping companies assess and hire developers based on their technical skills. The Y Combinator-backed startup now has more than 3,000 business customers, including Amazon, Nvidia, Clay, and Replit, and a community of over 30 million developers worldwide. Chakra represents a bet against the kind of technical assessment business HackerRank spent years building. Its traditional product largely tested whether developers could solve coding problems correctly. Nonetheless, Ravisankar believes AI has made HackerRank’s earlier model less useful to measure engineering ability. Ravisankar compared the transition internally to Apple moving from the iPod to the iPhone, as the old product still has value, but the new one represents where the startup believes the market is headed. “Chakra is going to be the headline,” he said. “It’s going to be the way that we’re going to move forward.”

articles.title: OpenAI launches visual ads that appear alongside image generation results | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The new ads will begin to appear later this month in the U.S. only for now, and will feature products and services from an initial test group of advertisers.
articles.body_text: ChatGPT is getting more ads. Specifically, OpenAI is adding visual display ads to its ad product line-up so that ads will appear alongside images that users ask ChatGPT to generate. In addition, the company is expanding its ad measurement tools and partnerships, and developing new ways to determine brand suitability. The new ads will begin to appear later this month in the U.S. only for now, and will feature products and services from an initial test group of advertisers. The ads will also be clearly labeled and won’t influence the answers ChatGPT provides, the company notes. The move follows the launch of Meta’s Muse, an agentic AI app which is free to everyone and a growing competitor for leading AI chatbots, like ChatGPT. OpenAI introduced ads earlier this year to support its free and low-cost subscription tiers, and expanded them to India in August. Now, the plan is to woo online advertisers who want to appeal to their potential customers by using more visual imagery to tell their stories. Eventually, those ads will allow them to target ChatGPT’s 1.2 billion weekly users, once they roll out globally. However, integrating such ads could also prove disruptive to the user experience. But perhaps that’s partly the point, as the ads could push more casual users to pay for a subscription in order to avoid them. Alongside the display ads, OpenAI said it is expanding its measurement tools and partner ecosystem, which now includes click attribution solutions, AppsFlyer, Triple Whale, Adjust, DV Rockerbox, Northbeam, Branch, Singular, Kochava, Airbridge, and Tenjin, as well as full-funnel, advanced measurement partners Fospha, Measured, and INCRMNTAL. OpenAI has also partnered with Haus, Measured, and WorkMagic to help advertisers explore “geo-based” experiments around ads. The company said it’s working on developing brand suitability evaluation pilots with help from DoubleVerify (DV) and Integral Ad Science (IAS), which will help advertisers better understand the ChatGPT ads environment. Combined, the moves see OpenAI working to make ChatGPT a viable ad-supported business for those on free and low-cost plans. articles.title: Google’s open-source bug bounty aims to clamp down on supply chain attacks
articles.summary: Google’s new program offers security researchers money if they find vulnerabilities in its open-source projects or the libraries those projects depend on.
articles.body_text: Google has introduced a new vulnerability rewards program to pay researchers who find security flaws in its open-source software or in the building blocks that its software is built on. It’ll pay anywhere from $101 to $31,337 for information about bugs in projects like Angular, GoLang, and Fuchsia or for vulnerabilities in the third-party dependencies that are included in those projects’ codebases. While it’s important for Google to fix bugs in its own projects (and in the software that it uses to keep track of changes to its code, which the program also covers), perhaps the most interesting part is the bit about third-party dependencies. Programmers often use code from open-source projects so they don’t continuously have to reinvent the same wheel. But since developers often directly import that code, as well as any updates to it, that introduces the possibility of supply chain attacks. That’s when hackers don’t target the code directly controlled by Google itself but go after these third-party dependencies instead. As SolarWinds showed, this type of attack isn’t limited to open-source projects. But in the past few years, we’ve seen several stories where big companies have had their security put at risk thanks to dependencies. There are ways to mitigate this sort of attack vector — Google itself has begun vetting and distributing a subset of popular open-source programs, but it’s almost impossible to check over all the code a project uses. Incentivizing the community to check through dependencies and first-party code helps Google cast a wider net. According to Google’s rules, payouts from the Open Source Software Vulnerability Rewards Program will depend on the severity of the bug, as well as the importance of the project it was found in (Fuchsia and the like are considered “flagship” projects and thus have the biggest payouts). There are also some additional rules around bounties for supply chain vulnerabilities — researchers will have to inform whoever’s actually in charge of the third-party project first before telling Google. They also have to prove that the issue affects Google’s project; if there’s a bug in a part of the library the company’s not using, it won’t be eligible for the program. Google also says that it doesn’t want people poking around at third-party services or platforms it uses for its open-source projects. If you find an issue with how its GitHub repository is configured, that’s fine; if you find an issue with GitHub’s login system, that’s not covered. (Google says it can’t authorize people to “conduct security research of assets that belong to other users and companies on their behalf.”) For researchers who aren’t motivated by money, Google offers to donate their rewards to a charity picked by the researcher — the company even says it’ll double those donations. Obviously, this isn’t Google’s first crack at a bug bounty — it had some form of vulnerability reward program for over a decade. But it’s good to see that the company’s taking action on a problem that it’s been raising the alarm about. Earlier this year, in the wake of the Log4Shell exploit found in the popular open-source Log4j library, Google said the US government needs to be more involved in finding and dealing with security issues in critical open-source projects. Since then, as BleepingComputer notes, the company has temporarily bumped up payouts for people who find bugs in certain open-source projects like Kubernetes and the Linux kernel.

GM’s Ultra Cruise will use radar, camera, and lidar to enable hands-free driving
articles.summary: GM revealed more details about its next-gen hands-free driving system, Ultra Cruise, announcing a sensor suite that includes radar, cameras, and lidar.
articles.body_text: General Motors’ next-generation Ultra Cruise driver-assist system will come equipped with lidar as well as several other high-tech sensors designed to enable hands-free driving and cover “95 percent” of driving maneuvers, the automaker announced today. In its first major update since announcing Ultra Cruise in late 2021, the automaker outlined several of the sensors that will power the driver-assist system, including cameras, short- and long-range radar, and a lidar sensor. The vehicles will also come with an all-new computer to process the data input from the sensors, which the automaker previously indicated would include Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon Ride Platform. According to a pair of diagrams provided by GM, the lidar will be located inside the vehicle, behind the windshield and under the rearview mirror, where other automakers typically install sensors for advanced driver-assist systems (ADAS). Cameras can be found on the sideview mirrors, short-range radar in the lower corners of the grille and rear bumper, and long-range radars underneath the hood ornament and beneath the taillights. “This will give us a 360-degree view around the vehicle to enable us to expand this hands free driving capability to these larger domains,” Jason Ditman, chief engineer at GM, told reporters in a briefing Monday. Ditman also said that drivers would be able to use Ultra Cruise “across nearly every paved road in the US and Canada.” [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/24484307/Ultra_Cruise_sensor_suite_front_view.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/24484306/Ultra_Cruise_sensor_suite_rear_view.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Lidar, a key ingredient in autonomous driving, is a laser sensor that uses near-infrared light to detect the shapes of objects. This helps autonomous vehicles “see” other objects on the road, like cars, pedestrians, and cyclists, all without the help of GPS or a network connection. GM first announced Ultra Cruise during an investor event in 2021, describing it as a massive leap over the company’s Super Cruise system, which allows for hands-free driving on mapped divided highways. In contrast, Ultra Cruise will cover “95 percent” of driving scenarios on 2 million miles of roads in the US, the company said. Now we’re getting more of a glimpse — albeit an extremely limited one — into the types of sensors and hardware that will be included in these Ultra Cruise-equipped vehicles. GM has said that the bespoke ultra-luxury Cadillac Celestiq would be one of the first vehicles to come with Ultra Cruise — but that vehicle isn’t expected to go into production until early 2024. GM hasn’t said which additional models will be compatible with the driver-assist system. Taken all together, these Ultra Cruise-equipped vehicles will be some of the most advanced cars ever produced by GM. The company is also developing the Ultra Cruise software in-house, using its own team of engineers and coders. Notably, the company is not partnering with Cruise, its robotaxi subsidiary, with Ditman calling the distinction between the two “unique.” Despite its enhanced capabilities, GM says it still considers Ultra Cruise a Level 2 system, as defined by the Society of Automotive Engineers. At Level 2, the vehicle can control both steering and acceleration and deceleration as well as monitor blind spots and even change lanes automatically. But the driver needs to stay vigilant and keep their eyes on the road; if they don’t, the vehicle’s infrared sensors will detect it, and the system will send several warnings to the driver before disengaging. Notably, that’s different from the Level 3 systems that Volvo, Mercedes-Benz, and Ford currently have under development. With a Level 3 system, a driver could theoretically take their eyes off the road under certain circumstances, like low-speed stop-and-go traffic. That said, GM intends Ultra Cruise to be its answer to other current Level 2 systems, like Tesla’s Full Self-Driving beta system. Tesla CEO Elon Musk famously shuns the use of lidar to power his company’s partially autonomous features, calling the laser sensor prohibitively expensive and a “crutch.” But as lidar costs fall, other automakers have embraced the hardware for its ability to render a 3D map of its environment and all nearby objects. In addition to GM, Volvo and Mercedes-Benz have recently announced their intention to include lidar in future production vehicles. And as Ditman put it, the decision to include lidar is less about money and more about safety. “The choice of our sensor set was really not predicated around cost,” he said. “It was really predicated around what do we think is needed in order to safely deploy this type of technology.” There is still a lot of research that needs to be done to fully investigate the safety claims made by automakers around ADAS features. There have been studies that show that the handoff between the automated system and a human driver can be especially fraught. When people have been disconnected from driving for a longer period of time, they may overreact when suddenly taking control in an emergency situation. They may overcorrect steering, brake too hard, or be unable to respond correctly because they hadn’t been paying attention. And those actions can create a domino effect that has the potential to be dangerous — perhaps even fatal. But Ditman argued that drivers need to feel confident, not complacent, about the ability of their vehicles to handle driving without their immediate input. “‘I’m not trying to drive complacency,” he said. “We addressed the inattentiveness with our driver attention system, so we don’t give you the opportunity to get complacent because if you do we’ll take the feature away from you.”

articles.title: Prinsessans stämning – på över 800 miljoner
articles.summary: Norska prinsessan Märtha Louise och hennes make Durek Verrett stämmer 14 personer och aktörer. I stämningen kräver de sammanlagt omkring 800 miljoner kronor.
articles.body_text: Norska prinsessan Märtha Louise och hennes make Durek Verrett stämmer 14 personer och aktörer. I stämningen kräver de sammanlagt omkring 800 miljoner kronor. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Stämningsansökan lämnades in i en domstol i Los Angeles i september. Prinsessan Märtha Louise, hennes make Durek Verrett och hans amerikanska bolag Ohana productions LLC anklagar sammanlagt 14 personer och aktörer för ärekränkning och för att ha brutit mot överenskomna sekretessavtal, rapporterar VG . Fyra personer namnges. Det handlar om en tidigare flickvän till Verrett, hans halvsyster Demetria de La Nuit, och två personer som tidningen beskriver som en tidigare manager och samarbetspartner samt en tidigare vän och samarbetspartner. Övriga tio personer eller aktörer har inte identifierats. I stämningsansökan yrkar Durek Verrett motsvarande över 300 miljoner kronor, Märtha Louise kräver över 200 miljoner kronor och bolaget över 300 miljoner kronor. Sammanlagt handlar det alltså om över 800 miljoner kronor, även om vissa krav kan överlappa varandra. Enligt domstolsdokumenten anser prinsessan och hennes make att de stämda länge spridit falska och skadliga påståenden om dem och att ryktesspridningen eskalerat de två senaste åren. – Våra klienters omdöme har i åratal dömts av allmänheten. Nu ska fakta prövas i en domstol, säger parets amerikanske advokat Richard Roth i ett uttalande till VG. Flera av de uttalanden som Durek Verrett hänvisar till har publicerats i norska Se og Hør. Förra året anmälde han tidningen till PFU, motsvarigheten till svenska Mediernas etiknämnd, för publicering av nakenbilder och anklagelser om övergrepp. Se og Hør fälldes i båda fallen. I stämningen hävdar Verrett att publiceringarna har fått stora ekonomiska konsekvenser för honom. Att hans intäkter har fallit rejält och på vissa områden mer eller mindre försvunnit. Även Märtha Louise hävdar att hennes affärsmöjligheter minskat kraftigt. – Jag såg just saken och tycker att det är en uppseendeväckande och speciell utveckling, särskilt så kort tid efter tronskiftet. Det ska bli mycket intressant att se grunden för parets stämningsansökan, säger Niklas Kokkinn-Thoresen, chefredaktör på Se og Hør, till VG. Detta är en nyhetsartikel. articles.title: Felicia, 17, var ombord på dödsbussen: ”Folk flög ut genom rutorna”
articles.summary: Felicia Arnmark Larsson, 17, var ombord på dödsbussen utanför Växjö. Hon satt på övervåningen och klarade sig med livet i behåll.
articles.body_text: Plötsligt kände Felicia Arnmark Larsson, 17, hur bussen körde in mitträcket – sekunder senare hängde folk i sina bälten. Hon satt på dödsbussen på väg från Växjö. – Det enda jag tänkte på var: Jag får inte dö. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. En ung man har dött och 14 personer har skadats allvarligt i bussolyckan utanför Växjö . Ett fyrtiotal personer var ombord. Många var ungdomar som reste hem till Ljungby efter en skoldag i Växjö. Felicia Arnmark Larsson, 17, var en av dem, vilket P4 Kronoberg var först med att rapportera om. Hon satt ensam i mitten på övervåningen i den fullsatta bussen när hon plötsligt hörde skrik. Bussen vinglade fram och tillbaka och plötsligt började den välta. – Jag kollade ut och såg hur vi slängdes ner mot marken och hur bussen voltade. Jag såg inte längre vägen och förstod då att det var kört. Det enda jag tänkte var: Jag får inte dö, jag får inte dö, säger hon. – Det var människor som kastades åt alla håll och kanter. Just då såg jag inte jättemycket men det var folk som flög ut ur rutorna, säger hon. Vissa hade säkerhetsbälte, andra inte. De som hade spänt fast sig hängde upp och ner, säger hon. Passagerarna på nedervåningen hade svårt att ta sig ut. Felicia Arnmark Larsson lyckades ta sig loss och ta sig ut genom takfönstret som gick sönder under kraschen. Det första hon såg var blodiga ansikten.

Islam Isaev, 16, skulle ha suttit på den aktuella bussen – men råkade ta fel. – Det är bra att jag gjorde det. Jag tycker synd om de som var på bussen, säger han. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. En dubbeldäckare i linjetrafik körde plötsligt av vägen klockan 16.30. Ombord på den satt ett 40-tal personer. Islam Isaev, 16, var på väg hem från skolan i Växjö när olyckan ägde rum. Jag var nära på att sätta mig på bussen, men jag råkade ta en annan buss från min skola, säger han och fortsätter: – Det är bra att jag gjorde det. Jag tycker synd om de som var på bussen. Bussen han tog i stället körde senare förbi olycksplatsen. Han såg hur bussen låg på sidan av vägen och att flera var skadade. – Några låg på marken. Många såg chockade ut. Det var läskigt, säger Islam Isaev. Polisen utreder olyckan och har under kvällen haft flera tekniker på platsen. Men vad som orsakat den är i nuläget oklart.

articles.title: Bolaget: Inget fel på olycksdrabbade bussen
articles.summary: En person har dött och ett tiotal skadats i allvarliga olyckan i Växjö. Enligt trafikoperatören fanns inga tekniska fel på bussen.
articles.body_text: Länstrafiken Kronobergs buss körde plötsligt av vägen utanför Växjö. En ung man har dött och ett tiotal personer skadats allvarligt. Enligt trafikoperatören fanns inga tekniska fel på bussen. – Senaste besiktningen var den utan anmärkningar, säger operativa chefen Andreas Ehrenborg. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Vid 16.30 körde tvåvåningsbussen av väg 25 utanför Växjö . Det var en buss från Länstrafiken som var i linjetrafik och körde sträckan Växjö till Ljungby. På den tvåfiliga vägen körde den plötsligt av vägen. En man i 18-årsåldern har dött och 14 personer är allvarligt skadade. Tio personer har vårdats på sjukhus i Kronoberg, och ytterligare fyra personer har förts till sjukhus i andra regioner. Två av de allvarligt skadade vårdas på intensivvårdsavdelning. Utöver dem har flera andra uppsökt sjukvård. Bussen ägs av bolaget Connectbus, som kör på uppdrag av Länstrafiken. Företagets operativa chef, Andreas Ehrenborg, säger att det är en oerhört tragisk olycka. – Tankarna går ju naturligtvis till alla som drabbats av detta på ett eller annat sätt. Det är naturligtvis en förfärlig olycka, säger han. Enligt polisen är busschauffören ”vaken och talbar” efter olyckan, men Connectbus har inte fått prata med honom än.

articles.title: Spelet bakom: Därför stänger Armémuseet
articles.summary: 8,7 miljoner kronor. Så mycket ville Statens fastighetsverk höja årshyran för Armémuseum på Östermalm i Stockholm. Nu lämnar museet de anrika lokalerna. – Lokalerna är begränsande, säger fastighetschefen Björn Hedin.
articles.body_text: Så mycket ville Statens fastighetsverk höja årshyran för Armémuseum på Östermalm i Stockholm. – Lokalerna är begränsande, säger fastighetschefen Björn Hedin. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. ■ Armémuseum lämnar Statens fastighetsverks lokaler på Östermalm efter en hyrestvist. ■ Bakom beslutet finns bland annat problem med lokalerna, och nu väntar jakten på nya. ■ Beskedet kom plötsligt, efter en tids dialog mellan parterna. Det var i mars som Statens fastighetsverk (SFV) sa upp hyresavtalet med Armémuseum på Östermalm i Stockholm , för att omförhandla hyran. I handlingar som Expressen har tagit del av framgår det att den föreslagna varmhyran – som skulle börja gälla 1 januari 2027 – låg på 23 061 000 kronor per år, mot 14 347 000 kronor i dag, vilket motsvarar en ökning på 60 procent. – Marknaden har gått upp väldigt mycket. För tre år sen (när nuvarande avtal ingicks, reds anm) hade vi inga indikationer på det, säger Ellinor Magnusson, fastighetsdirektör på myndigheten. Tidigare i år gjorde SFV en värdering med hjälp av två fastighetskonsultbolag, som jämförde med andra museer i närområdet. – Och då blev det den här nivån, och det är den marknadsmässiga nivån vi erbjuder. Sedan har man ju en diskussion med hyresgästen om man ska trappa upp hyran eller hur man gör, säger Ellinor Magnusson. Men Statens museer för maritim-, transport- och försvarshistoria (SMMTF), som driver Armémuseum, har inte gått med på den nya hyran.

articles.title: Styrkor till Saudiarabien
articles.summary: Jemenitiska regeringsstyrkor har återtagit kontrollen över det strategiskt viktiga sundet Bab al-Mandab, uppger Jemens militär. Pakistan och Turkiet skickar styrkor som stöd i den saudiska koalitionen som understödjer Jemens regering i striderna mot Huthirörelsen.
articles.body_text: Jemenitiska regeringsstyrkor har återtagit kontrollen över det strategiskt viktiga sundet Bab al-Mandab, uppger Jemens militär. Pakistan och Turkiet skickar styrkor som stöd i den saudiska koalitionen som understödjer Jemens regering i striderna mot Huthirörelsen. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Uppgifterna om återtagandet av kusten vid Bab al-Mandab kommer sedan en större motoffensiv mot den extremistiska, Iranstödda Huthirörelsen inletts i söndags. Enligt en talesperson för Jemens militär har dess styrkor skurit av vägen mellan staden Dhubab vid sundet och staden Mocka, och tagit kontroll över vägen. Hundratals stridande från Huthirörelsen har omringats i distriktet Dhubab, hävdar talespersonen. Över 1 000 räder har genomförts mot Huthimål, enligt Jemens militär. På måndagen tillkännages även en ”strategisk offensiv” mot den Huthikontrollerade huvudstaden Sanaa. Den saudiledda koalition som stödjer regeringsstyrkorna har på måndagsmorgonen använt 100 stridsflygplan i gryningsräder mot Huthirörelsen. Sent på måndagen meddelar både Turkiet och Pakistan att de skickar styrkor till Saudiarabien för att förstärka den militära koalitionen som strider i Jemen. Beskedet ges i ett gemensamt skriftligt uttalande från de tre länderna efter et möte i Riyad. FN:s generalsekreterare Antonio Guterres uppger samtidigt att han är ”djupt oroad över den kraftiga upptrappningen av striderna”. Den islamistiska Huthirörelsen intog Sanaa 2014 och har hållit huvudstaden sedan dess. Huthirörelsen har svarat med nya attacker mot Saudiarabiens energisektor, bland annat med en räd mot en oljeledning som leder till Röda havet. Sundet Bab al-Mandab förbinder Röda havet med Indiska oceanen, och kontrollen över farleden är därmed viktig för stora delar av den globala sjöfarten – inte minst sedan Hormuzsundet skurits av i och med Irankriget.

articles.title: Rök ihop om Trump – började skjuta vilt
articles.summary: David Mattai, 55, och Emmanuel Mathews, 80, rastade sina hundar i en park. De började gräla om Donald Trump var USA:s bästa eller sämsta president genom tiderna. Det slutade i vild skottlossning när båda drog sina vapen, rapporterar New York Times.
articles.body_text: David Mattai, 55, och Emmanuel Mathews, 80, rastade sina hundar i en park. De började gräla om Donald Trump var USA:s bästa eller sämsta president genom tiderna. Det slutade i vild skottlossning när båda drog sina vapen, rapporterar New York Times . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Snart väntar rättegång för det urartade Trumpgrälet som ägde rum i en hundrastgård i Bainbridge, Ohio , i april. Där satt Emmanuel Mathews, 80, som befann sig i parken med sin corgi, och läste Wall Street Journal vid ett picknickbord, rapporterar New York Times, som beskrivit händelsen utifrån de uppgifter som båda parternas advokater kunnat enas kring. En av tidningens rubriker var ”Trump tampas med rädslor för kriget”, med anspelning på Irankriget som då hade pågått i knappt två månader. – Det där suger, eller hur? sa då Jamie Jedlinsky, 70, som rastade sin hund i parken, och gestikulerade mot rubriken. Men Mathews höll inte med. I stället började han tala om sitt stöd för Trumps olika beslut med Jedlinsky, som skulle bli det enda ögonvittnet till den efterföljande konfrontationen. För medan de pratade dök David Mattai, 55, som beskriver sig som en ”demokratisk socialist”, upp med sin spaniel och gav sin syn på Trump. – Trump är den värsta presidenten någonsin, sa Mattai, som berättat att han kämpat mot alkoholism större delen av sitt liv och hade druckit under dagen. – Trump är den bästa presidenten genom historien, kontrade då Mathews.
